method_card.title: Frequency Polygons, Time Series and Line Charts
method_card.content:
A frequency polygon is drawn by plotting points at the midpoint of each class and the corresponding frequency, then joining consecutive points with straight lines. The most common error — flagged in examiner reports — is plotting at the class boundaries rather than the midpoint.

The midpoint of a class interval is found by averaging the two boundaries: \(\text{midpoint} = \frac{\text{lower boundary} + \text{upper boundary}}{2}\). For the class 20 ≤ x < 30, the midpoint is 25. This is the x-coordinate of the plotted point; the frequency is the y-coordinate.

A time series plots a variable against time (equally spaced time points on the x-axis). Points are joined in sequence. A trend line shows the overall direction; fluctuations above and below a trend line may indicate seasonal patterns. When describing a trend, include direction, rate of change, and any seasonal pattern.

A line chart is used for discrete data over time, where intermediate values between plotted points have no meaning. Both types must have labelled axes including units.

When comparing two frequency polygons on the same axes, comment on position (which has a higher mean), spread (which is wider), and — for Higher — shape (skew).
steps: Find the midpoint of each class interval: add the two boundaries and divide by 2
Join consecutive points with straight lines — do not curve or extend beyond the data
For time series, join points in time order and identify the overall trend direction
For comparisons, state a numerical comparison and interpret it in context

exam_context.marks: 2–4 marks; midpoint identification is 1 mark, reading values is 1–2 marks, comparison-in-context is 2–4 marks
exam_context.frequency: Frequency polygons appear on most papers; the midpoint plotting error is the most frequently penalised mistake in this topic

worked_examples.question: A grouped frequency table has classes 0–10, 10–20, 20–30, 30–40 with frequencies 4, 9, 13, 8. What coordinate (midpoint, frequency) should be plotted for the class 10–20?

steps.label: Step 2 — Write the coordinate
steps.content: The frequency for class 10–20 is 9. The coordinate is (15, 9).

worked_examples.question: A time series shows quarterly sales (thousands) for three years: Q1Y1: 8, Q2: 12, Q3: 15, Q4: 9; Q1Y2: 10, Q2: 14, Q3: 17, Q4: 11; Q1Y3: 12. Describe the trend and any seasonal pattern.

steps.label: Step 1 — Identify the trend
steps.content: The peaks (Q3 each year) rise: 15, 17. The troughs (Q1) rise: 8, 10, 12. Overall trend is increasing.

steps.label: Step 2 — Identify the seasonal pattern
steps.content: Sales peak each Q3 and fall in Q4/Q1. There is a clear annual seasonal pattern.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Overall increasing trend with a regular seasonal pattern: peaks in Q3, lowest in Q4/Q1 each year.

worked_examples.question: Two frequency polygons on the same axes show plant heights under two conditions. Group A peaks near x = 35 with a wider spread. Group B peaks near x = 50 with a narrower spread. Write a full comparison of the two distributions in context.

steps.label: Step 1 — Compare average
steps.content: Group B is centred higher (peak ~50 cm) vs Group A (peak ~35 cm). Group B plants are taller on average.

steps.label: Step 2 — Compare spread
steps.content: Group A has a wider, flatter polygon — more variation in height. Group B is narrower — more consistent.

steps.label: Step 3 — Interpret in context
steps.content: Plants under Condition B were typically taller by ~15 cm and more uniform, suggesting Condition B promotes more consistent growth.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Group B plants were taller on average (peak ~50 vs ~35 cm) and more consistent (narrower spread). Condition B promotes greater and more uniform height.

bronze.display: A class interval is 40 ≤ x < 50. What midpoint should be plotted on a frequency polygon?

misconceptions.message: Midpoint = (40 + 50) / 2 = 45. Never plot at 40 (lower boundary) or 50 (upper boundary).

bronze.display: A class interval is 15 ≤ x < 25. What is the midpoint?
A frequency polygon has points at (5,3), (15,8), (25,12), (35,7), (45,2). What is the highest frequency shown?

misconceptions.message: The highest frequency is the largest y-value. Here (25,12) has y = 12, which is the peak.

bronze.display: Which is the correct midpoint to plot for class 30 ≤ x < 50 on a frequency polygon?

misconceptions.message: Midpoint = (30 + 50) / 2 = 40. Plotting at 30 or 50 is the most common error.

bronze.display: A time series shows temperatures rising from 8°C in January to 22°C in July, then falling back to 9°C in December. Which term best describes this pattern?
options: A purely increasing trend
A seasonal pattern
A random fluctuation with no trend
A decreasing trend

misconceptions.message: The data rises and falls in a repeating annual cycle — this is a seasonal pattern.

bronze.display: A frequency polygon for exam scores has midpoints 5, 15, 25, 35, 45 with frequencies 2, 7, 11, 6, 4. At which midpoint is the modal class?

misconceptions.message: The modal class has the highest frequency (11). Its midpoint is 25.

bronze.display: A time series shows monthly sales: Jan 50, Feb 55, Mar 62, Apr 58, May 70. Between which two months did sales increase by the most?
options: January to February
February to March
March to April
April to May

misconceptions.message: Changes: +5, +7, −4, +12. The largest increase is April to May (+12).

bronze.display: A frequency polygon represents data in classes of width 10. The first midpoint plotted is x = 5. What is the lower boundary of this first class?

misconceptions.message: Lower boundary = midpoint − (class width / 2) = 5 − 5 = 0.

silver.display: A grouped frequency table has classes 0–20, 20–40, 40–60, 60–80. Which set of midpoints should be plotted?
A time series shows quarterly revenue (£000s): Q1: 42, Q2: 67, Q3: 85, Q4: 53. Calculate the change between Q3 and Q4.

misconceptions.message: Change = Q4 − Q3 = 53 − 85 = −32. The negative sign shows a fall.

silver.display: Two frequency polygons show weights of athletes. Sport A is centred ~75 kg with narrow spread. Sport B is centred ~85 kg with wider spread. Which comparison is correct?
options: Sport A athletes are heavier and more consistent
Sport B athletes are heavier on average but more varied in weight
Sport A is lighter but more varied; Sport B is heavier and more consistent
Both sports have similar average weights

misconceptions.message: Sport B is centred higher (85 vs 75 kg) = heavier average. Sport B also has wider spread = more variation. Both comparisons need context.

silver.display: A frequency polygon has a point at (35, 8) and the next at (45, 14). Estimate the frequency at x = 40 by linear interpolation.

misconceptions.message: Halfway between midpoints 35 and 45 is 40. Halfway between frequencies 8 and 14 is (8+14)/2 = 11.

silver.display: A time series for annual sales: 120, 135, 128, 150, 162 over 5 years. A trend line passes through (Year 1, 120) and (Year 5, 162). Estimate the trend-line value at Year 3.
A frequency polygon for commute times has midpoints 5, 15, 25, 35, 45 with frequencies 3, 10, 16, 8, 3. What is the total number of students?

misconceptions.message: Sum all frequencies: 3+10+16+8+3 = 40. Do not add the midpoints.

gold.display: Group X (n=40) has midpoints 10,20,30,40,50 with frequencies 2,6,14,10,8. Group Y (n=40) has same midpoints with frequencies 4,12,10,8,6. Which statement correctly compares the distributions?
options: Group X scored higher on average; Group Y was more consistent
Group Y scored higher on average; Group X had more students scoring above 30
Group X scored higher on average; Group X had more students scoring above 30
Both groups had identical average scores

misconceptions.message: Group X has more frequency at 30–50 (10+8=18 vs 8+6=14 for Y), so X scored higher on average. Check both the middle and the tails.

gold.display: A time series has 8 quarters: Q1Y1: 45, Q2: 60, Q3: 72, Q4: 50, Q1Y2: 52, Q2: 68, Q3: 80, Q4: 58. Calculate the first 4-point moving average.

misconceptions.message: First MA = (45+60+72+50)/4 = 227/4 = 56.75. Use exactly 4 consecutive values.

gold.display: Untrained group frequency polygon: midpoints 100,150,200,250,300 ms with frequencies 2,8,18,9,3. Trained group same midpoints: 1,5,10,14,10. Which statement correctly compares skewness?
options: The untrained group is skewed toward faster times; the trained group is symmetric
The trained group has more weight at higher reaction times, suggesting positive skew; the untrained group is more symmetric
Both distributions are symmetric with the same mean
The untrained group is negatively skewed; the trained group is positively skewed

misconceptions.message: Untrained peaks at 200 ms (roughly symmetric). Trained peaks at 250 ms with more weight at higher times — positive skew (tail toward higher reaction times).

gold.display: A time series trend line has equation y = 5x + 30, where x is the quarter number (starting at 1). What does the trend line predict for Quarter 12?
A student claims that because Group A's frequency polygon is always above Group B's, Group A must have a higher mean. Is this always true?
options: Yes — a higher polygon at every point always implies a higher mean
No — if A has more frequency at low x-values and B at high x-values, B could have the higher mean
No — the mean cannot be read from a frequency polygon
Yes — the polygon with greater area always has the higher mean

misconceptions.message: A polygon being higher at all points means more total frequency overall, but the mean depends on WHERE along the x-axis the frequencies sit. If A has more frequency at low values, B could still have the higher mean.

gold.display: Two frequency polygons represent heights of athletes. Distribution P has midpoints at 150, 160, 170, 180, 190 cm with frequencies 3, 9, 20, 12, 6 (total 50). Distribution Q has same midpoints with frequencies 5, 14, 15, 10, 6 (total 50). Which distribution has the higher mean?
options: Distribution P (weighted toward higher heights)
Distribution Q (higher early frequencies)
Both have the same mean
Cannot tell without calculating
